---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Material Frequency And Mix Consensus
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(SUB(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(prstkc, 0), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 0.01), 5), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(dvt, 0), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 0.01), 5)), RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(prstkc, 0), 3), TS_SUM(COALESCE(dvt, 0), 3)), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(prstkc, 0), 3), TS_SUM(COALESCE(dvt, 0), 3)))))
HYPOTHESIS: How often a firm runs a material repurchase rather than paying a material dividend and how much of its cumulative payout dollars went to repurchases are complementary readings of the same discretionary-payout philosophy, and averaging them measures that philosophy with least error.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The materiality-screened frequency contrast has the archive's most reliable alpha (0.051 with t=4.33) but the weakest slope of the leaders (FMB 3.19), while the dollar mix ratio has the strongest slopes (FMB above 4) and slightly lower alpha, so their errors appear to be partly offsetting. Combining them addresses the one remaining disagreement between the cross-sectional and portfolio evidence in the leading family rather than re-testing either element.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Asymmetric Threshold Payout Contrast
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUB(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(prstkc, 0), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 0.02), 5), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(COALESCE(dvt, 0), 0), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: The two payout channels should be screened asymmetrically because a repurchase only conveys a price opinion when it is large, whereas paying any dividend at all is already a binding commitment that removes flexibility.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Gen 7 showed materiality helps, and gen 7 also showed the dividend leg is indispensable since repurchase frequency alone earned alpha of -0.016 while the buyback-versus-issuance contrast earned -0.014. Raising the repurchase bar to two percent of market value while keeping the dividend indicator binary matches each screen to the economics of that channel, which should sharpen both portfolio legs simultaneously.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Three Year Buyback Minus Dividend Yield
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUB(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(prstkc, 0), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(dvt, 0), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho))))
HYPOTHESIS: Expressed as yields on market value, cumulative repurchases minus cumulative dividends measure the discretionary payout tilt in the same units as the valuation leg, so the interaction is dimensionally consistent and economically interpretable as a price-sensitive distribution rate.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The discretionary tilt has only ever been scaled by assets or converted into a bounded mix ratio, and asset scaling mixes a size and capital-intensity dimension into a signal that is fundamentally about price. Market-value scaling also keeps every payer in the sample, so this tests whether the strong alpha of the bounded mix can be attained at the higher coverage of a yield construction.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Dividend Burden Versus Buyback Activity
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(prstkc, 0), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 0.01), 5), NEG(RATIO(COALESCE(dvt, 0), oancf))))
HYPOTHESIS: The short leg works because dividends pre-commit cash flow, so the right measure of the dividend handicap is the share of operating cash flow already pledged to shareholders as dividends, not merely whether a dividend exists.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive established that shorting habitual dividend payers is the essential ingredient, but it has never measured how binding that habit is relative to the firm's cash generation, which is the economic content of the constraint. Replacing the dividend count with a payout-ratio burden while keeping the material repurchase count as the long-side channel tests a genuinely different formulation of the same mechanism.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Dual Value Anchor With Material Frequency
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), SUB(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(prstkc, 0), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 0.01), 5), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(dvt, 0), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 0.01), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Combining earnings yield with book-to-market gives a broader cheapness reading that should strengthen the cross-sectional slope, and pairing it with the material payout-composition contrast should retain the abnormal return that book-to-market alone could not deliver.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Book-to-market produced the strongest FMB slopes but near-zero alphas, while earnings yield produced the alphas, which suggests the two anchors carry complementary information: one about price relative to accounting capital, one about price relative to profits. Averaging them by rank directly targets the residual weakness of the leading signal, whose FMB slope of 3.19 is below the best in the archive.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Smoothed Earnings Yield With Payout Contrast
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(MA(ib, 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUB(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(prstkc, 0), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 0.01), 5), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(dvt, 0), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 0.01), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheapness should be judged against normalized rather than single-year earnings, because a temporarily depressed or inflated profit figure misclassifies firms whose price is actually reasonable, and management's payout behavior is set with reference to normal earning power.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The valuation leg has repeatedly proven decisive in this family, yet it has always used one year of income, which is the noisiest available version of the concept and mechanically induces annual reshuffling of the long portfolio. A three-year average of income keeps the profitability content that sales-to-price lacked while making the anchor more stable, which should raise the alpha t-stat and the spread Sharpe together.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
